# SHB-07 FPGA top-up explicit coverage

Authority: [SHB revision 1.1](../../014-Shop-SHB-Proposal-Revision-2026-10-30.md), including Appendix A. Phase 10's 10-01 slice is advanced inline with one explicit test; parent completion counts remain11/42 and 1/14 until actual gates qualify. Real company inputs/adoption remain pending in the single [decision register](../decisions.md).

## Invariant

SHB-07: "Eligible FPGA purchase and later top-up — No routine engineer approval; each accepted paid order records its own purchased hours once and is available to staff; no online balance update."

Operational translation: when SLL re-invites an existing customer for a top-up, the second purchase runs through the ordinary automatic eligible-FPGA checkout. Each PaidOrder is independent: its own primary key, its own `order_reference`, its own purchased hours, its own purchase-notice delivery. There is no cumulative total maintained by the application; there is no automated time credit (no `SyntheticFulfilment` or `SyntheticSupportEvent`), consistent with the deferred "SLL manually tracks used/remaining hours and manually emails each task outside the shop" posture.

## Verification

`test_eligible_fpga_top_up_records_independent_paid_orders_per_invitation` in `backend/shop/shb/paid_order_tests.py` exercises the full lifecycle:

1. The fixture customer completes an FPGA purchase (3 × 10h = 30h, `shb-fpga-10h`) through the invitation created by `setUp`.
2. The staff issuer calls `discounts.issue_fixture` to create a second invitation for the same customer with the same `Synthetic Company Limited` company name and a `SLL top-up` project reference.
3. The customer activates the new invitation on the existing browser session via `/invite/<token>`.
4. The customer runs the standard review → checkout → pay sequence with quantity 2 (20h).
5. The test asserts: two `PaidOrder` rows with distinct primary keys and distinct `order_reference` values, hours 30/20 respectively, `variant_id='shb-fpga-10h'` on the first (and implicitly matching on the second via the form default), `support_tracking='manual-outside-shop'` on both, `effects_authorized=False` on both, exactly two `PurchaseNoticeDelivery` rows, zero `SyntheticFulfilment`, zero `SyntheticSupportEvent`.

The invariant was already implicit in the existing checkout and paid-order wiring. This commit makes it explicit so a future refactor cannot silently introduce an aggregating "balance" field or an automated support-time credit.

Shared regression passes **608 tests** (previously 607; +1 for SHB-07): 265 SHB, 95 access/recovery, 104 payment, 30 staff, 24 worker/statement-mail, 75 shared transaction/archive, nine source/catalog and six actual network-isolated adapter cases. Django check, migrations 0029/0030 and drift pass with no new drift. [Current regression/source record](../evidence/shb/retained-tests/f5ae15048343dd4f4d6aa355379c8c83fcdf30caf1f34237f74323735117311d.json); focused 1-test audit record [ad265762…json](../evidence/shb/retained-tests/ad265762332aeda016aa3dc77e5b5fec5f930456fbabf68acd6c719f5ccbfbc5.json). Browser lane is unchanged at 161 checks (71 customer/90 staff, JS/no-JS at 320px); the top-up assertion is backend-only and does not change any customer- or staff-visible behavior.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 scripts/check_shb_retained.py --test-label shop.shb.paid_order_tests.PaidOrderTests.test_eligible_fpga_top_up_records_independent_paid_orders_per_invitation
python3 scripts/check_shb_retained.py --shared
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_planning_activity.py'
python3 scripts/check_purchase_plan.py --refresh-inventory
python3 scripts/check_planning.py
python3 scripts/check_purchase_plan.py
```
